name: Boston
title: How to Get Rid of a Couch, Mattress or Furniture in Boston (2026 Guide)
meta_description: Every verified way to get rid of a couch, mattress, furniture or appliance in Boston: City curbside & mattress pickup, ReStore, furniture banks, and paid haulers, with rules, costs and sources.
intro: Boston has free City options for furniture, mattresses and appliances, but each has its own rules. Here's what each option takes, what it costs (only where they publish it), and where we got the information.

quick_answers.a: If you get City curbside trash collection, furniture can go out next to your bins on your regular collection day. To donate instead, check the ReStore and furniture banks below; most require clean, undamaged pieces.

Mattresses are banned from Massachusetts trash. In a building with 6 units or fewer, book the City's curbside mattress pickup appointment (the City page mentions no fee). In 7+ units, use your property manager or one of the mattress haulers below.
Book a City special item collection. Remove fridge doors and all food first.

quick_answers.q: Can't carry it to the curb?
quick_answers.a: City pickups are curbside only. Paid options that come inside include ReSupply (donation pickup), LoadUp, and several mattress haulers.

listings.condition_rules: Put furniture out with your normal curbside trash and recycling on your scheduled collection day, placed neatly next to your trash receptacles. Trash must be curbside by 6 a.m.; don't put it out before 5 p.m. the evening before. The City does not collect construction debris, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, fences, or auto parts.
listings.stairs_inside: No. Curbside only; the City will not pick up on private property.
listings.lead_time: Your regular trash collection day (find it in the Trash Day app or the City's schedule search).
listings.cost: No fee is mentioned on the City page. Check with 311 if unsure.
listings.service_area: Addresses that receive City of Boston curbside trash collection. Large buildings (7+ units) should check the City's large-building page and their property manager.
listings.name: City of Boston curbside furniture collection

items_not_accepted: Other non-mattress items (these can go out with curbside trash)
listings.condition_rules: Appointment required; mattresses are not collected with regular trash (Massachusetts waste ban). Soiled, dirty, or bed-bug mattresses must be bagged and fully sealed. Do not crush or cut the mattress. Place curbside by 6 a.m. on your appointment day (or after 5 p.m. the night before), not blocked and with nothing on top. Limit: 10 items per calendar year. Cancel before 12 p.m. the day before.
listings.stairs_inside: No. Curbside only; items on private property are not collected.
listings.cost: No fee is mentioned on the City page. Check with 311 if unsure.
listings.service_area: City of Boston residents in buildings with 6 units or fewer. Buildings with more units must use their property manager or a private hauler.
listings.name: City of Boston curbside mattress & box spring recycling (appointment)

items_not_accepted: Dishwashers, water heaters, plumbing fixtures (donate or hire a private hauler)
listings.condition_rules: Appointment required. Remove all fridge/freezer doors (including mini-fridges) and all food, or the item won't be collected. Don't smash appliances or electronics. Wipe data from computers. TVs and computers must be freestanding, not boxed. Max 5 items per appointment and 10 per calendar year. Cancel before 12 p.m. the day before.
listings.stairs_inside: No. Place it where trash is collected (curbside, public alley, or dumpster area); items on private property are not collected.
listings.cost: No fee is mentioned on the City page. Check with 311 if unsure.
listings.service_area: City of Boston residents.
listings.name: City of Boston special item collection (fridges, ACs, TVs, monitors)

listings.condition_rules: All donations must be in working order. Staff can refuse any item based on condition and store need. Email the ReStore for the current list.
listings.stairs_inside: Drop-off: staff help unload at the store. In-home pickup is arranged through ReSupply (paid; see the ReSupply listing).
listings.lead_time: Drop-off Tuesday to Saturday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (as posted).
listings.cost: Drop-off fee: not stated. Pickup is through ReSupply, a paid service.
listings.service_area: Drop-off at the West Roxbury store. Habitat says a second ReStore is set to open in Watertown in fall 2026.
listings.name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Boston ReStore (West Roxbury)
items_accepted: Tables & chairs (not conference tables or dated)
Upholstered furniture (not ripped, worn, broken, dated or faded)
Appliances less than eight years old (fridges, washers, dryers, free-standing stoves, cooktops, microwaves, never-installed dishwashers)

listings.notes: Habitat Greater Boston ReStore and Household Goods both point donors to ReSupply for in-home pickup.
listings.condition_rules: Items should be clean, sturdy, complete, and usable (no broken frames, missing parts, or pet damage). Items the charity can't accept may carry a recycling fee, charged in $10 increments.
listings.stairs_inside: Yes. Teams go up and down stairs; disassembly is available. Extra fees may apply.
listings.lead_time: Priority pickups in 24 to 48 hours; small items in as little as one hour (per ReSupply's Boston page).
listings.cost: Paid service. Starts at $19 (bags/boxes), $49 (small furniture and boxes), $99 (sofas and bulky furniture), plus a separate non-refundable booking fee. Final quote confirmed on site before loading.
